name: Silver dapple
summary: Silver dapple (PMEL17): dilutes black pigment only, toward chocolate on the body and near-flaxen on the mane and tail, while leaving red untouched. A black becomes chocolate with a pale mane, a bay becomes silver bay, and a chestnut carrying it looks unchanged - it has no black to act on.

phenotypes.name: Silver dapple
phenotypes.description: Black pigment walked toward chocolate, and most of the way to flaxen on the mane and tail, with red untouched - a chocolate body under a pale mane on a black horse, silver bay on a bay. A chestnut carrier looks unchanged.

conditions.name: Ocular cysts (silver)
conditions.description: One silver copy. Small cysts sit at the back of the iris. Common in silver horses and usually harmless - but it is the same defect that disables a horse with two copies.

conditions.name: Multiple congenital ocular anomalies
conditions.description: Two silver copies. The eyes are malformed - cysts and a misshapen cornea - and the horse is a little frailer for it.
